To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

rock phosphate enriched organic fertilizer (RP enriched organic fertilizer) with phosphate solubility microorganisms (PSM) improved the production of legume by increasing the nodulation, growth and yield of legume.
RP enriched organic fertilizer containing PSMs can be used as an alternative source of phosphorus for the optimum production and yield of legume crops.

the application of RP enriched organic fertilizers with PSMs could improve soil properties (e.g., aggregate stability and P release), nodulation, growth and yield of chickpeas and lentils, and thus could be an effective and sustainable approach to increase the production of leguminous crops in the P deficient soils.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of a sustainable and environment friendly technology for the production of leguminous crops in the developing countries where the use of inorganic fertilizer is not feasible due to economic and environmental constraints.
the production of legume crops using RP enriched organic fertilizer and PSMs.
the use of RP enriched with organic fertilizer and PSM to increase P availability for legumes production and to reduce the use of chemical fertilizer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
RP enriched organic fertilizer is a promising alternative for DAP for the production of legume crops.
RP enriched organic fertilizer containing PSMs could be used as an alternative to DAP for the production of legume crops.
the use of RP enriched compost with PSMs could produce results similar or better than DAP in terms of growth and yield of chickpeas and lentil.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
RP enriched organic fertilizer is a potential alternative to chemical fertilizer for the production of legume crop.
the use of RP enriched with organic fertilizer and PSMs is a promising approach to enhance P availability and legumes production.
the use of organic fertilizer with P-solubilizing bacteria is a promising strategy to increase the yield and quality of chickpea and lentil in the P-deficient soils.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of RP enriched fertilizer PSM can be a sustainable option for the production of legume crops in the long term.
the use of P-rich organic fertilizer in combination with PSMs could be an alternative to the chemical fertilizer to improve soil P availability, and legume production.
the use of rock phosphate enriched organic fertilizer along with phosphate solubiling microorganisms is a viable alternative to diammonium phosphate.
